notes:
Read-along now reads each balloon in the order it is printed.

Speech bubbles are lettered centre-aligned, so a short line starts further right than a long one — and the app was sorting a balloon's own lines left to right. It read them in order of line width. "I'm sorry to keep interrupting, but I cannot stay in one place for too long" came out as three sentences in the wrong order. That is fixed.

It also stops deleting things. Shouts and laughter were being thrown away in silence — WHAAAT?!, AKIRAAAA!, HAHAHA, DIE! DIE! — because anything not on a short internal list was dropped, while untranslated Japanese sound effects were read out. Both sides were backwards.

And a line printed once is spoken once: repeated balloons are now matched by where they sit on the page rather than by their spelling, which is what the text reader gets wrong.

Found by transcribing a real chapter on a device and comparing it to the pictures, rather than by listening.
